goal: Contain and report every source-side per-file open, hydration, read, resume, size-drift, and unrepresentable-name failure without corrupting framing or aborting the remaining transfer.
recommended_approach: Adopt contract v7 with stable manifest-entry IDs, an opened-source abstraction exposing handle metadata, exact-length shard preparation, and explicit per-entry states; make file records chunk-framed and terminal-status-aware across control, data-plane, and relay sinks; stage full-file destination writes beside the target and atomically commit only after a successful terminator, preserving any prior destination on failure.
comparison: The plan selects the right core mechanisms and substantially improves its first revision through a need ledger, per-file preparation outcomes, resume handling, terminators, and post-read validation, but its in-place rollback, zero-padding, relay lifecycle, source-handle interface, and path-as-identity choices prevent it from being the best approach.
material_changes: Stage full-file writes and atomically replace the destination only after a successful record terminator; abort must preserve an existing destination.
Replace data-plane zero padding with chunk-framed records whose terminator can follow any successfully transmitted byte count.
Redesign TransferSink around begin/write/commit-or-abort semantics and require DataPlaneSink to forward failed terminators through relay routes.
Add an opened-source-file abstraction that exposes metadata from the same handle used for reading.
Use a stable manifest-entry ID for grants, records, skips, and ledger keys; keep bounded or lossy paths only for destination naming and reporting.
Move local open-failure acceptance into ssc-4 or retire the local availability pre-check in ssc-1 so every slice can pass its claimed guards independently.

findings.title: A failed record deletes the previous destination copy
findings.evidence: docs/plan/SOURCE_SIDE_CONTAINMENT.md:262-266 and :361-365 — discard removes the active path and explicitly expects a pre-existing decoy to be overwritten and then removed; crates/blit-core/src/remote/transfer/sink.rs:876 — the current streamed sink creates and truncates that path directly.
findings.predicted_failure: If a source read fails while updating an existing backup file, the transfer reports a skip but destroys the last good destination copy, leaving no file until a successful rerun.
findings.better_approach: Write full-file records to a uniquely named sibling staging file, apply metadata there, and atomically replace the target only after an OK terminator; abort removes only the staging file.

findings.title: Zero padding can turn one read failure into file-sized wasted I/O
findings.evidence: docs/plan/SOURCE_SIDE_CONTAINMENT.md:253-256 and :452-455 — a failed data-plane record pads the unread remainder with zeros, potentially up to the complete manifest size.
findings.predicted_failure: An early read error on a very large file can force gigabytes or terabytes of zero transmission and temporary disk writes, causing stalls or disk exhaustion and preventing subsequent files from landing.
findings.better_approach: Frame the data-plane body as bounded length-prefixed chunks followed by a terminal status; validate that successful records total header.size while allowing failed records to terminate immediately.

findings.title: The terminator design does not cover relay sinks
findings.evidence: docs/plan/SOURCE_SIDE_CONTAINMENT.md:245-267 — terminators and discard behavior are specified for filesystem, local, and null sinks; crates/blit-core/src/remote/transfer/sink.rs:2022-2038 — DataPlaneSink currently relays a header and body through send_file_from_reader and immediately reports success; crates/blit-core/src/transfer_session/mod.rs:6061-6126 — the sink API receives only the body stream, not its terminal outcome.
findings.predicted_failure: In a remote-to-remote relay, an upstream short read or failed terminator leaves a partial downstream record whose relay returns an error or desynchronizes, aborting the session instead of propagating a contained per-file failure.
findings.better_approach: Make record completion part of the TransferSink lifecycle so DataPlaneSink can forward the same success or failure terminator downstream and filesystem sinks can commit or abort their staged write.

findings.title: Same-handle drift validation is not expressible through TransferSource
findings.evidence: docs/plan/SOURCE_SIDE_CONTAINMENT.md:269-276 and :329-352 — the design requires metadata checks on the opened handle before and after reading; crates/blit-core/src/remote/transfer/source.rs:184-188 — open_file returns only Box<dyn AsyncRead + Unpin + Send>, which exposes no metadata operation.
findings.predicted_failure: An implementation that falls back to path-based metadata can inspect a replacement inode rather than the file actually read, producing false retractions or finalizing bytes whose opened file changed undetected.
findings.better_approach: Return an OpenedSourceFile abstraction containing the reader and a same-handle metadata method, with fault-injecting implementations for tests and explicit relay behavior.

findings.title: A bounded lossy display path remains the protocol identity
findings.evidence: docs/plan/SOURCE_SIDE_CONTAINMENT.md:63-67 keeps lossy strings as manifest identity, while :235-243 bounds skip paths to MAX_FAILURE_PATH_BYTES; crates/blit-core/src/remote/transfer/sink.rs:188-191 truncates reported paths, and crates/blit-core/src/remote/transfer/payload.rs:200-203 collapses headers in a HashMap keyed by relative_path.
findings.predicted_failure: A long granted path cannot be matched by its truncated skip, and an invalid-byte filename colliding with a legitimate U+FFFD filename can overwrite that file's planning entry, causing a protocol abort, an unreported file, or the legitimate file to be skipped.
findings.better_approach: Assign every manifest entry a stable opaque ID echoed by NeedEntry, payload records, skips, and terminators; retain the exact source PathBuf behind that ID and use the string path only for representable destination naming and bounded display.

findings.title: The first slice cannot prove its claimed local behavior
findings.evidence: docs/plan/SOURCE_SIDE_CONTAINMENT.md:389-404 says the current local availability pre-check intercepts open failures and can make mirror fatal, but :465-474 assigns local A3 containment to ssc-1 while removing that pre-check only in ssc-4 at :483-489.
findings.predicted_failure: The ssc-1 local open-failure guard cannot pass with its claimed exit-2 containment semantics, so the plan cannot land each slice independently green as required.
findings.better_approach: Either retire the availability pre-check in ssc-1 or move local A3 implementation and acceptance to ssc-4.
